figures.finding: Pitcairn has no employment ordinance and no age of employment or performer's rule; the Children Ordinance (a child: under eighteen) only makes whoever runs a workplace (where goods are made for sale, roads or buildings built, public works done or heavy machinery used) keep children out where the work could harm their health, safety or morals, and bars children from bars unless supervised. A film set or stage is a workplace only if it falls within those kinds. Nothing distinguishes a young writer or director.

value.workplaceDuty: operator keeps children out of harmful workplaces (manufacture for sale, construction, public works, heavy machinery)

figures.applies: Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno Islands; UK Acts in force there ('applied Acts') weren't traced (see majority in layer 3).

sources.said: 10A. It shall be the duty of all persons who have responsibility for the operation of workplaces: (a) to determine whether the operation of that workplace or the nature of the work involved is likely to harm the health, safety or morals of children, and if so determined to then ensure that no children are in that workplace;

(2) In this Ordinance “workplace” means any place in which: (a) goods (including food) are manufactured for sale or trade; (b) construction of roads, buildings or other structures is being undertaken; … (d) heavy machinery is being used for any purpose
child means a person under the age of [18] years;

sources.title: Children Ordinance, Cap. 41 (revised edition 2014), Laws of Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno Islands, Government of the Pitcairn Islands
